newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway expected to pass new oil, gas projects - agency.
newsitem.headline: Norway expected to pass new oil, gas projects - agency.

text.p: Norway's parliament is expected to give the go-ahead on Tuesday for the development of three oil and gas fields in the North Sea, the national NTB news agency said.
Parliament is due to vote on the plans later on Tuesday but NTB said the political parties already had agreed on the proposals and the vote was just a formality.
The three developments are Jotun, the remaining part of the Troll development and Oseberg South.
The Jotun oilfield, operated by Esso Norge, comprises three separate structures -- Elli, Tau West and Elli South -- which will be developed as one production unit.

Total reserves are estimated at about 200 million barrels of oil equivalent. Oil production is due to start in 1999 and to last 16 years with plateau production of around 80,000 barrels a day (bpd) of crude between 2000 and 2002.
The field lies in blocks 25/8 and 25/7, about 200 km west of Stavanger on the west coast of Norway and 29 km north of Esso's Balder field.

Partners in block 25/8 are Esso and Enterprise Oil Norge with 50 percent each. Partners in block 25/7 are Norske Conoco with 37.5 percent, Amerada Hess with 12.5 percent and Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) with 50 percent.
NTB said parliament also would clear the remaining sections of the Troll prospect, which is expected to yield around 91 million cubic metres of oil and 46 billion cubic metres of gas.
Throughput at the development will be about 180,000 bpd until 2016, NTB said.

Output at Oseberg South is planned to begin in 2000 and peak at 124,000 bpd a year later. Recovereable reserves at the field are estimated at 53.5 million cubic metres of oil and 11 billion cubic metres of gas, the news agency said.
Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA is operator of both Troll and Oseberg South.
